description: Team AstroByte unites developers and data enthusiasts tackling climate challenges. Through EarthWatch AI, we use NASA Earth-observation data and machine learning to track deforestation, water depletion, and land changes to empower planetary action.
summary:
EarthWatch AI is a fully responsive, client-side web application built as an interactive 3D geospatial dashboard for monitoring environmental indicators, weather anomalies, and ecosystem health using real-time satellite data.

Designed with a modern glassmorphism UI, it combines a WebGL-powered 3D globe with live data streams from NASA and open-source geographic services.
details:
EarthWatch AI is an interactive, browser-based geospatial intelligence platform designed to monitor environmental changes, weather anomalies, and ecosystem health in real time.

  • How it works:
    • It renders a fully interactive 3D globe (Globe.gl / Three.js) that allows users to spin, zoom, and inspect any location on Earth.
    • When a user taps a location or searches for a region, the application queries live satellite and meteorological data sources—including the NASA POWER API (for daily precipitation and root-zone soil wetness) and the MODIS MOD13Q1 API (for Normalized Difference Vegetation Index / NDVI data).
    • It processes these live metrics through a rule-based analytical engine to evaluate indicators like flood risk (scored out of 100), vegetation loss, and drought stress, displaying the results in a sleek side panel or mobile bottom sheet.
    • It also supports dynamic NASA GIBS WMS overlays to project active thermal anomalies (fires), rain rates, and vegetation layers directly onto the 3D globe surface
  • Democratized Access to Earth Data: Translates complex, raw scientific datasets from NASA into easily digestible visual indicators, making earth observation data accessible to students, researchers, and the general public without requiring heavy GIS software.
  • Instant Risk Assessment: Provides immediate multi-parameter breakdowns (7-day rainfall, 30-day rainfall, wettest day, soil saturation, and vegetation change over 5 years) for any coordinate on the planet.
  • High Reliability & Offline Resilience: Built with robust fallback mechanisms; if NASA servers experience latency or network connectivity drops, the app seamlessly switches to high-fidelity sample datasets and schematic textures so the user experience is never interrupted.
  • Responsive Multi-Device Layout: Features a mobile-optimized bottom sheet layout and a desktop glassmorphism sidebar interface that adapts seamlessly to any screen size.
  • Disaster Awareness & Preparedness: Helping local communities, environmental analysts, and stakeholders quickly identify developing flood risks or drought stress in vulnerable regions (such as delta areas or agricultural belts).
  • Climate Change Transparency: Raising awareness of long-term environmental shifts, such as vegetation decline and deforestation, by allowing users to compare current ecological health with historical baselines.
  • Educational Engagement: Serving as an interactive learning tool for schools and universities to explore geography, climatology, and satellite telemetry hands-on.

  • Development Environment & Software: Visual Studio Code, web browsers with hardware-accelerated WebGL support, and local testing servers.
  • Zero-Install Geospatial Powerhouse: Packing a fully featured 3D satellite visualization and telemetry dashboard into a lightweight, single-page web architecture that runs entirely in the browser without plugins.
  • Dynamic Texture Composition: Instead of relying on static background images, the application dynamically draws and merges NASA base maps and thematic WMS raster overlays on an offscreen HTML5 canvas before feeding the texture to the 3D globe engine.
  • Regional Aggregation Modes: Features specialized analytical views—such as the India State-by-State Overview—that concurrently query capitals across entire nations, plotting color-coded risk nodes directly on the globe and ranking them in real time.
  • Performance & Frame Rates: Optimizing WebGL rendering loops, geometry merging, and asynchronous API calls to ensure smooth 60fps globe rotation and snappy UI responses even when fetching data for multiple regions.
  • User Experience & Clarity: Designing an intuitive interface using modern glassmorphism principles where scientific numbers are paired with color-coded risk pills (Low, Moderate, High) and plain-language summaries rather than confusing jargon.
  • Graceful Degradation: Factoring in potential network constraints by building robust timeout handlers and offline sample fallback states, ensuring the application remains fully functional under any network condition.
